---
title: "Node keys"
---

Scripts and edit files refer to nodes by their key, not by their node ID.
A key follows from the source data, so it stays the same when the node IDs change: with another library version, or when a node is added or removed elsewhere in the model.
A node ID is the next free number, and nothing may depend on its value.

## The key of a node

The key is in the node column `meta_key`, and is unique in the model of a water authority.
In the coupled model a node is identified by its authority, `meta_waterbeheerder`, and its key.
A key is set when the node is created, and does not change after that, also when the type of the node changes or another Basin is merged into it.

| Node | Key | Example |
|:-----|:----|:--------|
| Connector node on a structure | the code of the structure | `GA1-st9` |
| Connector node on open water, gravity controlled | `ow:` and the code of its hydroobject | `ow:KD25.1_0` |
| Boundary, gravity controlled | `bnd:` and its ID in the boundaries layer | `bnd:28` |
| Basin, gravity controlled | `up:` and the key of the connector node it drains through, the smallest if it has several. Without one, `down:` and the connector node that feeds it | `up:GA1-st9` |
| RWZI | `rwzi:` and its code | `rwzi:30021` |
| Observation, UserDemand | the node type and its name | `observation:NL27_KD_3` |
| Storing (bergend) Basin, and the node that connects it | `bergend:` and `bergend_link:` with the key of the Basin it stores for | `bergend:up:GA1-st9` |
| Control or demand node | the node type and the key of the node it controls, the smallest if it controls several | `discrete_control:GA1-st9` |
| Junction | `junction:<from>><to>#<n>x<m>`: the smallest key of the n nodes that flow into it, and of the m nodes it flows to | |
| Any other node | its location in whole metres | `loc:152150,365169` |

Equal keys get a number, `@1`, `@2`, in an order that follows from the data: along the hydroobject, or by location.

`ribasim_nl.keys.lumped_keys` sets the keys of the gravity controlled input models.
`Model.write` gives the nodes without a key one with `ribasim_nl.keys.fill_keys`, by the rules from the RWZI down in the table, and checks that every node has a key and that no two are equal.
The keys of the Junctions are set again every time, since their trees are rebuilt along the way.

## Refer to a node

In a script, right after the model is read:

```python
model = Model.read(ribasim_toml)
# nodes and links are referred to by their key, see docs/dev/node-keys.qmd
n = model.node_id
lk = model.link_id

model.merge_basins(node_id=n("up:ow:SG1_0"), to_node_id=n("up:DO1-st3"))
model.reverse_link(link_id=lk("up:KS52-st2", "KS52-st2"))
```

`n` returns the ID of the one node with a key, and raises a `KeyError` if there is none or more than one.
A link has no key: `lk` returns the ID of the link between two nodes.
In the coupled model pass the authority as well: `model.node_id("KGM056", authority="Noorderzijlvest")`.

- **Model edits.** A layer of `model_edits.gpkg` refers to a node in a column `<name>_key`, which `Model.apply_edits` passes to the argument `<name>_id` of the edit method: `node_key`, `to_basin_key`. It refers to a link in the columns `link_from_key` and `link_to_key`. The layer `add_basin` gives the new Basin a key in its column `key`.
- **`static_data.xlsx`.** The sheets `Pump`, `Outlet` and `Basin` refer to a node in their column `key`.

## Add a node

A node that a script adds gets a key by the rules above when the model is written, or when a key is looked up that no node has yet.
Give it a key yourself where it is referred to later, so that the reference reads well:

```python
model.outlet.add(Node(geometry=Point(152150, 365169), meta_key="inlaat-keersop"), tables=[...])
```

A node that replaces another one, such as a FlowBoundary that becomes a LevelBoundary, gets the key of the node it replaces.

## Not a node ID

Not every integer in a script is a node ID.
Row numbers of source layers (`fid_as_index=True`), codes of areas, capacities and levels stay as they are.
Refer to a row of a source layer by its code where it has one.
